issue_body:
This is the epic that includes all the steps for the import migration, plus the smaller follow-ups that were deliberately deferred out of the big PRs.

The import engine was recreated from scratch to be more modern: better validation, a new phase system (dynamically defined by each entity importer so it adapts to any complexity), and persistence based on CQRS commands. That intermediate refacto landed in PR #42247 and is the prerequisite for finishing step 1.

**`.ai/Component/Import/PLAN.md` is the source of truth** for the architecture (decision log, contracts, schema) until the migration reaches GA — where an issue body and the plan differ, the plan wins.

## Roadmap (execution order)

- [x] **Engine refinements** — `ImportMessage` rows refactor (small PR, first), then the `ProductRowImporter` split. **Both merge before step 1 restarts** — see #42422
- [ ] **Step 1 — CQRS run lifecycle + phase sequencer** (rework of the frozen PR #41911, product entity only): #41907
- [ ] **Step 2 — remaining entity importers** (categories, combinations, customers, addresses, brands, suppliers, aliases, store contacts): #42136
- [ ] **Step 3 — Symfony wizard UI** (step-1/step-2 screens + progress modal behind the `import` flag): #42137
- [ ] **Step 4 — UI tests + GA** (Playwright campaigns, then flag promotion — gated by the performance go/no-go): #41922
- [ ] **Transactions** (case-by-case per importer, waits on #42250): #42385
- [ ] **Known limitations** (deferred by design, schedule-independent): #42423
- [ ] **Job owner** (employee / API client) recorded through `MutationTracker`, no import schema change: #42956
- [ ] **Post-wizard evolutions** (perf mitigation, validation-time creation preview, product field gaps, deprecated-code removal at next major): #42424

issue_title: SF Migration - Import - Step 1: CQRS run lifecycle + phase sequencer (PR2)
issue_body:
> Part of the Import admin page migration epic #42357 (spike by @tleon in #41321). Supersedes #41798 and #41799.
>
> **This issue was rewritten (2026-08) after the import engine landed in #42247.** The original body described a pre-engine design (session-held wizard state, `ImportBatchReport`, per-batch `shared_data`, int entity types, no phase model) that the engine superseded. **`.ai/Component/Import/PLAN.md` is the source of truth** for the architecture (decision log, contracts, schema deltas) until the migration reaches GA.

## Goal

Rework the frozen step-1 PR #41911 into the CQRS layer on top of the import engine (#42247): the `ImportRun` lifecycle commands drive the engine's phase sequencer, and `ps_import_run` persists the run state so batches are resumable with no client-posted blob.

**Scope: the PRODUCT entity only.** Even though the frozen baseline reached categories through the deprecated legacy handlers, `CategoryImporter` and every other entity belong to step 2 (#42136). The `ps_import_run` rework however lands **here** and must anticipate the future scenarios: string `entity_type` open to any registered importer (module importers included), `current_phase`/`phase_totals` supporting arbitrary per-importer phase lists (e.g. a category `finalization` phase, a combination `attribute_generation` phase), and `options` JSON round-tripping importer-specific keys untouched (PLAN decision 26).

**Prerequisite:** the two engine refinements tracked in the "Engine refinements" sub-issue of #42357 (the `ImportMessage` rows refactor, then the `ProductRowImporter` split) merge first, so this PR integrates a stable engine surface.

## What the engine already provides (#42247)

`EntityImporterInterface` + registry (module-extensible), `ImportRunContext` (single runtime object), pausing-phase model, file normalization to a canonical working file (separator and skip rows consumed there), cursor-based batch resume, `ProductImporter` covering the 66 legacy columns, finders/resolvers with the ambiguity policy, and the integration suite. This PR adds **no importer logic** — it wires runs, persistence and sequencing around the engine.

## Tasks

- [ ] **Phase sequencer** in `RunImportBatchHandler`: drop the deprecated `Core\Import\Importer` / `ImportHandlerFinder` reliance; budget loop over `countPhaseUnits()` / `processPhaseBatch()`; one batch may span a phase boundary; completion = the last phase's offset reaching its total (no "short batch" heuristic).
- [ ] **Pause flow**: a pausing phase completing with ≥ 1 warning or error stops the run as `awaiting_confirmation` (notices never pause); re-calling `RunImportBatch` implicitly accepts and resumes; `CancelImportRun` rejects; `options.dryRun` truncates the phase list after `validation` (API validate-only — a dry run with errors still ends `finished`).
- [ ] **One state shape**: `RunImportBatch` returns the same `ImportRunState` DTO as `GetImportRunState`; `ImportBatchReport` is dropped. Status lifecycle: `pending → running ⇄ awaiting_confirmation → finished | cancelled | failed`.
- [ ] **`StartImportRun`**: normalize the upload once into the run-scoped working file (`<runId>.work.csv`, canonical dialect); compute phase totals from the measured data-record count; build the run's **single-shop `ShopConstraint`** + run-start guard (a group-/all-shops scope fails once, legibly — PLAN decision 24); truncate option executes once at `database` phase entry, never in dry run.
- [ ] **`EntityType` → string ids** end-to-end (PLAN decision 14): removes the Domain → `Core\Import\Entity` int leak; `entity_type` column becomes a string.
- [ ] **Structured messages**: `messages` JSON (`{severity, phase, rows, field, message}`) capped at 1 000 per severity + `message_counts` for the overflow; **message coalescing** (equal messages merge, rows cumulate) implemented here where the cap lives — the DTO shape arrives from the engine-refinements sub-issue.
- [ ] **Schema deltas** on `ps_import_run` (details in PLAN.md): add `current_phase`, `resume_cursor` (opaque reader cursor), `phase_totals` JSON, `skipped_rows` JSON, `messages`/`message_counts` JSON; drop `validate_only` (→ `options.dryRun`); decide the likely drop of `shared_data` (phases are stateless); settle **standalone columns vs the `options` blob** field by field (criterion in PLAN.md: query/filter/per-batch-write targets stay columns; frozen read-back-whole config folds into `options`). `db_structure.sql` only — upgrade SQL only if the flag ships enabled somewhere.
- [ ] **Constants**: invalid-row sanity cap (~10 000 → run fails as malformed), GC retention (~7 days).
- [ ] **Cleanup & GC**: terminal status clears `skipped_rows`/`resume_cursor` and deletes the working file (capped messages kept for the report); opportunistic purge of old terminal runs in `StartImportRunHandler` + a `prestashop:import:purge-runs` console command (core has no cron).
- [ ] **Concurrency**: keep the per-run non-blocking Symfony Lock from #41911 (`FlockStore`, fail fast → `ImportRunAlreadyRunningException`); settle the cancel-vs-lock interplay and the `failed` status (sanity cap breach / fatal error / stored phase id no longer matching `getPhases()`).
- [ ] **Behat** (the engine's CQRS importers need no web context — the blocker recorded on #41911 is gone): feature files for run lifecycle, product create (basic fields), product update (`forceIDs` / `match_ref`), accessories incl. mutual A↔B, pause/confirm/cancel, skip behavior + sanity cap, dry run; one fixture CSV per scenario family under `tests/Resources/import/`, every mapped column asserted.

## Out of scope

- Other entity importers → #42136 (step 2). Wizard UI → #42137 (step 3). UI tests + GA → #41922. Transactions → #42385. Removal of `AdminImportController` and the deprecated classes → next major (tracked in the post-wizard-evolutions sub-issue of #42357).
- `ps_import_match` mapping presets stay a BO-only helper on the existing `ImportMatchRepository` — no CQRS layer (unchanged from the original refinement).

| Questions         | Answers
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------
| Type?             | improvement
| Category?         | BO
| Sponsor company   | @PrestaShopCorp

| Questions         | Answers
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------
| Branch?           | develop
| Description?      | Adds the **Version-branch bootstrap** workflow (1st-priority candidate from #41818). When a new version branch is opened (e.g. `develop` → `9.2.x`), this manually-dispatched, `prestashop-sa`-gated workflow (1) creates the version branch if it does not exist yet, then (2) opens/updates **one idempotent PR per repository** — core, `test-scenarios`, `presthubot`, `kanbanbot`, `TranslationTool`, `ga.tests.ui.pr` — adding the new branch to each repo's CI matrices / branch lists. Version, target branch and minor/major are **derived from `src/Core/Version.php`** (no release inputs); the only inputs are `dry_run` (default `true`) and a `target_owner` fork-test override. Edits are **ADD-only** (two version branches cohabit during stabilization; old ones are cleaned up manually) and **re-runnable**: an already-applied change opens no PR, an open PR is updated, a closed one is ignored (a fresh PR is created). A final job reports every PR for maintainers to review and merge manually (the workflow never merges). The team gate and PR idempotency reuse the patterns from `create-build-branch.yml` and `create-merge-pr.yml`.
| Type?             | improvement
| Category?         | PM
| BC breaks?        | no
| Deprecations?     | no
| How to test?      | Dispatch **Version-branch bootstrap** from a fork with `target_owner=<fork-owner>` and `dry_run=true`: the run gates on the `prestashop-sa` team, derives `9.2.x` from `Version.php`, and prints the per-repo diffs + a PR report **without** pushing. Re-run with `dry_run=false` to open the PRs on the forks; re-running stays idempotent (no duplicate PRs; a closed PR yields a new one). Transform idempotency is independently checked by running each `.github/release-bootstrap/transform-*.sh` twice and asserting an empty second-run diff.
| UI Tests          | N/A
| Fixed issue or discussion?     | Implements a candidate from #41818 (does not close it)
| Related PRs       | The sibling-repo PRs are opened automatically by the workflow run.
| Sponsor company   | N/A

The passed form options should be validated; the format itself is, by essence, very large and can include many things. We can't validate its format directly because we can't guess it

However, we do know the associated form type, so we should be able to try to build this form type by passing the form options. The form type itself is able to interpret and validate the passed options via its config resolver, so a validation based on this system should be doable

It should be integrated in:
- the registry when a module registers a new property
- in the CQRS commands when they are created from the BO (since the registry already handles it internally from the previous point, maybe we could rely on it; however, validating early in the command handler would prevent starting some updates that are not correct)

title: Add the version-branch bootstrap workflow
issue_title: Release automation: candidate new GitHub workflows
issue_body:
## Context

As part of improving the PrestaShop release process, we reviewed the full release procedure against the workflows that already exist (in this repo and in `smb_edition_builder`) to identify **manual steps that could become GitHub Actions**. This issue is the candidate list.

The read-only **release healthcheck** (what-to-check catalogue) is tracked separately in #41804 and should be done **first**; this issue is only about the *new semi-automation* workflows. It deliberately also records what we considered and decided **not** to build, so those aren't re-proposed.

## Already automated (coverage map — for reference, not to redo)

- Version bump + build/version branch → `create-build-branch.yml`
- Changelog + contributors PR → `generate-changelog-pr.yml`
- OS ZIP archive → `build-release.yml`; nightly → `cron_nightly_build.yml` (GCS upload)
- Module/composer updates (cron) → `cron_php_update_modules.yml` (excludes `psgdpr`, `ps_apiresources`)
- FOS JS routing (cron) → `cron_js_routing.yml`
- Merge-up PRs → `create-merge-pr.yml` / `cron_create_merge_prs.yml`
- Translation fixtures check → `check_prerelease.yml`
- Classic build/deploy → `smb_edition_builder`: `build-classic-archive`, `deploy-classic*`, `prepare-classic-edition-branch`, `cron_bump_modules`
- Docker images → automatic PR on `PrestaShop/docker` (next-day), then `publish.yml`
- Autoupgrade label/diff tracking → `create_diff_for_autoupgrade_pr_label.yml` + verify/notify

## Proposed new workflows (prioritized)

| Order | Workflow | Repo | Automates | Trigger / inputs | Output |
|-------|----------|------|-----------|------------------|--------|
| **1st** | **Version-branch bootstrap** 🔒 | orchestrator (core + sibling repos) | "Open PRs in multiple repositories" when creating a version branch | `workflow_dispatch(new_version, base=develop)` | batch of PRs across core, `test-scenarios`, `presthubot`, `prestashop.github.io`, `kanbanbot`, `ga.tests.ui.pr`, `TranslationTool` |
| **2nd** | **Update hooks bundle** | core (+docs, autoupgrade) | "Update the hooks" | `workflow_dispatch` (manual, **not** cron) — inputs: version, devdocs path, autoupgrade path | up to **3 PRs when relevant**: (a) core `hook.xml` fixtures, (b) devdocs-site hooks doc, (c) autoupgrade SQL |
| candidate | **Create GitHub release (draft)** 🔒 | core | "Prepare the GitHub release" | `workflow_dispatch(sha/branch, version, changelog source, prerelease)` | a **draft** release: tag at the chosen sha + changelog body (publishing stays manual — human go) |
| candidate | **Classic config preparation** | `smb_edition_builder` | Classic build config steps | `workflow_dispatch(core_version, classic_dist_version)` | auto-create `config_classic_<ver>.yml` from the branch config + open the PR, pre-filling the `stepgit` label |

> 🔒 **Restricted to the `prestashop-sa` team.** **Version-branch bootstrap** and **Create GitHub release (draft)** are critical and must gate on team membership exactly like the existing `create-build-branch.yml`: a first `check-membership` job (which every later job `needs:`) that calls `https://api.github.com/orgs/PrestaShop/teams/prestashop-sa/memberships/${{ github.actor }}` with the `JARVIS_TOKEN` secret (`read:org`) and fails (`exit 1`) on any non-`200`. Reuse that job verbatim. *(The healthcheck in #41804 is read-only and needs no such gate.)*

### Implementation note for "Update hooks bundle"

The autoupgrade SQL command (`prestashop:update:sql-upgrade-file-hooks-listing`) today can only **append the whole new hook list** — it **cannot update** the SQL script when a previous query block was already added. This needs improving before/alongside this workflow. Proposal: wrap the generated block in **comment markers** (e.g. `-- BEGIN/END auto hooks <version>`) so the workflow can detect and **replace** the prior block instead of duplicating it.

## Considered and intentionally dropped

- **Lock themes version / Release & pin API module** — done manually; the healthcheck (#41804, checks B4/B5/B6 + F3/F4) verifying the pins & published tags is enough.
- **Archive upload** — not needed.
- **Autoupgrade max-version PR** — done manually by another team.
- **Distribution-API release-note PR** — done manually by another team.
- **Translation extract + push-to-Crowdin orchestration** — the two existing manual workflows are fine as-is (the wording PR must be merged before pushing to Crowdin, so they can't be chained into a single run anyway).
- **Post-release healthcheck** — folded into the #41804 healthcheck (its post-release section runs on every healthcheck run).
- **Release-tracker issue sync / dedicated security private-build workflow** — not needed.
- **Addons marketplace version registration & compatibility** — can't be automated (the marketplace tooling is too old; must be done manually via the Updator UI).

---

*Related: #41804 (release healthcheck — what-to-check catalogue).*

title: Replace legacy extra-property validation with Symfony Validator constraints
issue_body:
So far the field validation is only based on legacy `Validate:*` functions, like in ObjectModel. We need to improve this so we can also use assert Constraints, like in doctrine and ApiResources:
- impacts on the definition structure in DB
- refacto of the extra property validation service so it should be based on SF constraints only
- to get similar rules as legacy ones usually TypedRegex does the job, so we'd better force constrints all the time
- with constraints we can have multiple errors for multiple fields much more easily
- for the form, constraints should be added on the relevant fields
- the ExtraPropertyCQRSApiValidator should be refactored, now it should be able to handle multiple violation errors simply by using the validate method

Also remember to remove the auto-added `NotBlank` constraint in `ExtraPropertiesFormBuilderModifier`. Now that we can configure constraints properly, this should be left to the responsibility of the module/developer

issue_title: [Quick Access] Replace native prompt() dialog with a proper modal when adding a quick access link
issue_body:
**As** a back office user,  
**In order to** configure a quick access link properly when adding the current page,  
**I want** the native browser `prompt()` dialog to be replaced by a PrestaShop modal that lets me set the shortcut name **and** choose whether it opens in a new window.

---

## Context

### Current behaviour

When the user clicks **"Add current page to QuickAccess"** in the Quick Access dropdown, the BO triggers a native browser `window.prompt()` dialog:

```
Please name this shortcut: [________________]
```

This dialog:
- Is a **native browser UI element**, unstyled, inconsistent across browsers, and cannot be customised or translated contextually
- Offers **only a name input** — no way to set the "Open in new window" option at creation time
- Blocks the JavaScript thread in some contexts
- Cannot be tested reliably with Playwright (requires `page.on('dialog')` workarounds)

The relevant code is in:
```
admin-dev/themes/default/template/header.tpl
```
```javascript
var name = prompt('Please name this shortcut:', '{$quick_access_current_link_name.0|truncate:32}');
```

The Quick Access listing page (`Manage quick accesses`) already allows setting the "Open in new window" toggle when creating or editing a link. This option is **not exposed** at all in the dropdown "add" flow today, leading to a feature asymmetry.

### New behaviour

Clicking "Add current page to QuickAccess" opens a **PrestaShop modal** (using the existing `@PrestaShop/Admin/Components/Modal/` Twig component or the equivalent UIKit modal) containing:

- A **text input** pre-filled with the current page name (same default as the current `prompt()`)
- A **toggle switch** labelled "Open in new window" (defaulting to `off`)
- A **"Save"** button that submits the form via AJAX and closes the modal
- A **"Cancel"** button (or close icon) that dismisses the modal without action

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC-1 — Modal opens on click

- Clicking "Add current page to QuickAccess" in the Quick Access dropdown opens a PrestaShop modal.
- The native `window.prompt()` is no longer called anywhere in this flow.
- The modal is accessible (focus trap, `aria-modal`, `role="dialog"`, labelledby title).

### AC-2 — Name field

- The modal contains a text input labelled "Shortcut name" (or equivalent wording).
- The field is pre-filled with the current page name, truncated to 32 characters (same logic as the current `prompt()` default).
- The field is focused automatically when the modal opens.
- The field is required — the "Save" button is disabled (or inline validation is shown) when the field is empty.

### AC-3 — "Open in new window" toggle

- The modal contains a toggle switch labelled "Open in new window".
- The toggle defaults to **off**.
- When toggled on, the saved quick access link opens the page in a new browser tab (i.e., `new_window = 1` is sent to the AJAX endpoint).

### AC-4 — Save action

- Clicking "Save" submits the data via AJAX to the existing `AdminQuickAccesses` / Symfony `QuickAccessController` endpoint (same as the current flow, extended with the `new_window` parameter).
- On success:
  - The modal closes.
  - The dropdown list is refreshed to include the newly added link.
  - A success alert/flash is shown consistent with existing BO UX.
- On error:
  - The modal stays open.
  - An inline error message is shown.

### AC-5 — Cancel / close

- Clicking "Cancel" or the modal close icon dismisses the modal without creating a quick access link.
- The dropdown remains in its current state.
- Pressing `Escape` also dismisses the modal.

### AC-6 — Wording

The following wording keys are added to the `Admin.Navigation.Header` translation domain:

| Key | Default EN value |
|---|---|
| `Add to Quick Access` | `Add to Quick Access` (modal title) |
| `Shortcut name` | `Shortcut name` |
| `Open in new window` | `Open in new window` |
| `Save` | reuse existing key |
| `Cancel` | reuse existing key |

### AC-7 — No regression on existing quick access behaviour

- "Remove from Quick Access" still works as before (no modal, direct AJAX action).
- "Manage quick accesses" link still navigates to the listing page.
- Existing links in the dropdown still navigate correctly (incl. `new_window` behaviour).
- The `new_window` field in the Create/Edit form on the listing page is unaffected.

### AC-8 — AJAX endpoint compatibility

- The existing AJAX endpoint used by the "add" action (`action=GetUrl&method=add`) accepts the additional `new_window` parameter.
- If the Symfony-migrated controller (`QuickAccessController`, PR #41508) is in place, the endpoint on that side also handles the `new_window` parameter correctly.

---

## Technical Notes

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| File to modify (legacy header) | `admin-dev/themes/default/template/header.tpl` |
| Current mechanism | `window.prompt()` → AJAX to `AdminQuickAccesses?action=GetUrl&method=add` |
| Modal component | `@PrestaShop/Admin/Components/Modal/` or UIKit `ps-modal` |
| Toggle component | `SwitchType` Symfony form type / UIKit `ps-switch` |
| Translation domain | `Admin.Navigation.Header` |
| Related PR (listing page migration) | [#41508](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/41508) |

**Implementation notes:**

- The modal should be rendered server-side as a Twig include in `header.tpl` (or the equivalent Symfony Twig component for the migrated header), and shown/hidden via JavaScript — avoid generating the modal HTML dynamically in JS.
- The AJAX request to save the quick access link already exists. It only needs to be extended with the `new_window` parameter from the toggle value.
- If the Symfony Layout component for the header is already in use, implement the modal there rather than in the legacy `header.tpl`.
- The pre-filled name truncation (32 chars) is currently done in Smarty (`{$quick_access_current_link_name.0|truncate:32}`). Ensure the same truncation is applied in the Twig/JS equivalent.

---

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Native `window.prompt()` is removed from the "Add current page to QuickAccess" flow
- [ ] A PrestaShop modal opens with a name input (pre-filled, required) and an "Open in new window" toggle (default off)
- [ ] Save submits via AJAX with both `name` and `new_window` parameters, and the dropdown refreshes on success
- [ ] Cancel / Escape closes the modal without side effects
- [ ] Wording keys are added to `Admin.Navigation.Header` translation domain
- [ ] No regression on existing quick access dropdown behaviour (remove, navigate, manage)
- [ ] The modal is accessible (focus trap, ARIA attributes)
- [ ] A UI test covers the new modal flow (open, fill name, toggle new_window, save, verify link appears in dropdown)

issue_body:
# EPIC — Native Extra Properties System

> **Discussion:** [#40767](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/discussions/40767)  
> **Main PR:** [#41092](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/41092) (Kiwik contribution)  
> **Architecture:** [`src/Core/ExtraProperty/ARCHITECTURE.md`](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/src/Core/ExtraProperty/ARCHITECTURE.md)  
> **Sponsor:** KIWIK

---

## 1. Objective & Opportunity

PrestaShop ships with a large number of native fields on its core entities (Product, Order, Customer, etc.), but no merchant's needs are ever fully covered by defaults. Today, a module developer who needs to attach extra data to an entity faces a grim menu of workarounds:

- Altering core DB tables directly (breaks upgrades, pollutes schema)
- Creating standalone extra tables with no framework integration (invisible to the API, to grids, to forms)
- Repurposing existing fields like `note` or custom text fields (semantically wrong, not typed)
- Using the legacy hook-based approach for each layer independently (FO template, BO form, grid, API — four separate integrations to write)

**This Epic introduces a first-class extra properties system** that allows any module to register typed, schema-managed extra fields on any PrestaShop entity — surfaced automatically in the front-office (Smarty LazyArrays), Symfony back-office (forms + grids), and Admin API, without touching a single core table and without writing integration plumbing for each layer.

### Why it matters

- **Merchants** stop needing hacky overrides for basic business needs (ERP code on a product, accounting email on a customer, priority flag on an order)
- **Agencies & module developers** get a safe, upgrade-proof extension point with a single registration call
- **Interoperability**: extra fields from one module can be read and displayed by another
- **Headless / API-first**: extra data is automatically visible in the Admin API — a prerequisite for modern frontends and integrations
- **Community**: reduces the #1 open-source complaint of "I can't add extra fields without hacking core"

### Target outcome

A module developer can express `Module::registerExtraProperty('product', 'video_link', ...)` once in `install()`, and the field is immediately:

1. Stored in a dedicated schema-managed table (`ps_product_extra_lang`)
2. Readable/writeable via ObjectModel (`$product->getExtraProperty('mymodule', 'video_link')`)
3. Exposed in Smarty (`{$product.extra_properties.mymodule.video_link}`)
4. Editable in the BO product form (auto-appended field, correct Symfony form type)
5. Visible in product grids (opt-in via `display_grid` flag)
6. Available in the Admin API (`GET /products/{id}` → `extraProperties.mymodule.video_link`)

---

## 2. What Has Already Been Done — PR #41092

PR #41092 by Kiwik (Jeremie-Kiwik) implements the majority of the architecture described in `ARCHITECTURE.md`. The following tasks from the original list are covered.

### ✅ Task 1 — Module registration API (`Module.php`)

`classes/module/Module.php` exposes three public methods:

- `registerExtraProperty(string $entityName, string $fieldName, ExtraPropertyOptions|array $options)`
- `unregisterExtraProperty(string $entityName, string $fieldName, string $fieldScope, bool $dropColumn)`
- `unregisterExtraPropertyById(int $idExtraPropertyDefinition, bool $dropColumn)`

The registration pipeline resolves through `EntityExtraFieldRegistryInterface` → `CachedExtraPropertyRegistry` → `ExtraPropertyRegistry`, which orchestrates:

- Schema creation/alteration via `ExtraPropertySchemaManager` (`ENSURE TABLE + ADD COLUMN`)
- Conflict detection via `UNIQUE KEY (entity_name, module_name, field_name)` in the definition registry
- Definition persistence in `ExtraPropertyDefinitionRepository`

All three basic types (String, Int, Bool) are handled, as well as Float, DateTime, Choice (enum with JSON-encoded choices array), and Json — through the `ExtraPropertyType` backed enum and `ColumnDefinitionMapper`.

### ✅ Database & schema infrastructure

Central registry table `PREFIX_extra_property_definition` is created at install time (added to `install-dev/data/db_structure.sql`). Key columns include: `field_type`, `field_scope`, `module_name`, `storage_column_name`, `symfony_field_type`, `property_path`, `sql_index`, `validator`, `display_front`, `display_api`, `display_bo`, `display_grid`, `grid_position`, and i18n wording pairs.

Dynamic value tables are created on first registration per entity: `{entity}_extra` (common scope), `{entity}_extra_lang` (lang scope), `{entity}_extra_shop` (shop scope).

### ✅ Task 2 — ObjectModel integration (Legacy PHP)

`ObjectModel` gains four public methods:

- `getExtraProperties(?string $moduleName = null): array`
- `getExtraPropertiesByModule(?string $moduleName): array`
- `getExtraProperty(?string $moduleName, string $propertyName, ?string $scope = null): mixed`
- `setExtraProperty(?string $moduleName, string $propertyName, mixed $value, ?string $scope = null): void`

Reads go through `ExtraPropertyReaderInterface` (three-scope `SELECT`). Writes are triggered by `ObjectModel::save()` via `persistExtraProperties()` → `ExtraPropertyWriterInterface` (three-scope `UPSERT`). The ServiceLocator is used in the legacy context (no Symfony DI in ObjectModel).

### ✅ Task 2b — Front-office LazyArray presenters

`AbstractLazyArray` gets a `getExtraProperties()` method that delegates to an `ExtraPropertiesLazyArray` instance assigned by the concrete subclass. The following LazyArrays are wired:

- `ProductLazyArray` (including cart/listing via `CartProductPresenter`)
- `CategoryLazyArray`, `SupplierLazyArray`, `ManufacturerLazyArray`, `StoreLazyArray`
- `OrderLazyArray`, `OrderDetailLazyArray`, `OrderReturnLazyArray`

Smarty template access:

```smarty
{$product.extraProperties.mymodule.video_link|default:''}
{$order.extraProperties.mymodule.is_priority|default:false}
```

Exposure is filtered by `display_front = 1`. A two-tier cache (Symfony pool + `FilesystemAdapter` fallback) avoids repeated definition reads in FO contexts where `cache.app` is absent.

> **Note:** `CartLazyArray` does **not** expose `extraProperties` on the cart entity itself — this is an explicit gap (see US-EP-02 below).

### ✅ Task 3 — Admin API integration

Extra properties are exposed in read operations under an `extraProperties` sub-object, filtered by `display_api = 1`. Write operations go through the CQRS bus (`UpdateExtraPropertyValuesCommand`). The API mapping uses the `storage_column_name` → camelCase convention configured at registration time.

### ✅ Tasks 4 & 5 — Back-office Form and Grid integration

`ExtraPropertiesFormBuilderModifier` auto-appends extra property fields at the end of any migrated Symfony form. The Symfony form type is derived from `symfony_field_type` (stored at registration). Labels are translated at runtime via wording/domain pairs (`translator->trans($wording, [], $domain)`).

`ExtraPropertiesGridDefinitionModifier` injects extra columns into Symfony grids. The `grid_position` integer controls column placement; `display_grid` gates visibility. Filtering and sorting on extra properties columns are supported.

### ✅ Task 6 — All supported types

The `ExtraPropertyType` enum covers: `String`, `Int`, `Bool`, `Float`, `DateTime`, `Choice` (backed by a JSON-encoded choices array), and `Json` (auto-encoded/decoded on read/write).

title: Merchandaise return ui tests
issue_title: [UI Tests] Adapt Merchandise Returns UI tests for Symfony-migrated controller
issue_body:
# [UI Tests] Adapt Merchandise Returns UI tests for Symfony-migrated controller

## User Story

**As** a Core team member,  
**In order to** ensure the Symfony-migrated Merchandise Returns page is covered by automated UI tests,  
**I want** the existing UI test files for Merchandise Returns to be adapted so they pass with the feature flag `merchandise_returns` enabled (Symfony controller), and the feature flag promoted to `stable` once all tests pass.

---

## Context

The **Merchandise Returns** page (`Customer Service > Merchandise Returns`) is a two-surface feature in the PrestaShop BO:

### 1. The listing page

Lists all RMA (Return Merchandise Authorization) requests submitted by customers, with filter, sort and pagination. Also includes a configuration section at the bottom to enable/disable returns, set the validity period, and configure the return prefix.

### 2. The edit page

Allows the shop manager to update the status of a return request and view the returned products list. Accessible by clicking on a return in the listing.

Both surfaces were handled by the legacy `AdminReturnController`. The full Symfony/CQRS migration is introduced by [PR #41527](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/41527) by `tleon`, which builds on top of an earlier partial migration (listing was already partially migrated — see issue [#23609](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues/23609)). The migration is gated by the feature flag `merchandise_returns`.

### Existing tests

Existing UI test files are located at:

```
tests/UI/campaigns/functional/BO/05_customerService/02_merchandiseReturns/
```

These tests cover the full workflow: enabling returns in the options section, filtering and sorting the listing, and editing a return status. They do **not** need to be rewritten — only adapted to the new Symfony selectors, form rendering, and URLs introduced by PR #41527.

> **Note:** The campaign test has an impact on another page (order detail page) :
> ```
> tests/UI/campaigns/functional/BO/02_orders/01_orders/viewAndEditOrder/06_merchandiseReturns.ts
> ```

### Goal

Adapt the existing test files under `05_customerService/02_merchandiseReturns/` so that all scenarios pass against the **Symfony-migrated controller** when the feature flag `merchandise_returns` is enabled, without breaking the existing legacy path (flag disabled).

### Scope of changes

The following scenarios must pass against the Symfony implementation introduced by PR #41527:

| Scenario | Current coverage | Adaptation needed |
|---|---|---|
| Navigate to Merchandise Returns listing | Legacy `AdminReturn` URL | Update URL assertion to Symfony pattern |
| Filter returns by ID, order reference, customer name, date | Legacy filter form | Update filter form selectors to Symfony grid |
| Sort returns by column | Legacy sortable table | Update sort selectors to Symfony grid |
| Pagination controls | Legacy paginator | Update pagination selectors |
| Enable/disable returns (options section) | Legacy configuration form | Update options form selectors and save action |
| Set return validity period | Legacy input | Update selector to Symfony form field |
| Set return prefix | Legacy input | Update selector to Symfony form field |
| Navigate to edit a return | Legacy edit URL | Update URL pattern and navigation selectors |
| Update return status | Legacy edit form | Update status dropdown and save selectors |
| Success flash messages | Legacy alerts | Verify Symfony flash message selectors |

### Acceptance Criteria

> **Pre-condition:** Feature flag `merchandise_returns` is enabled in `Advanced Parameters > New & Experimental Features`.

**AC-1 — Page object adaptation**
- Page objects used by the test files (`tests/UI/pages/BO/customerService/merchandiseReturns/`) are updated to match the selectors of the Symfony-migrated listing, options form, and edit page introduced by PR #41527.
- Legacy selectors (flag disabled) remain functional without regression.

**AC-2 — Listing page (flag enabled)**
- Filtering by ID, order reference, customer name, and date returns the correct results on the Symfony grid.
- Column sorts (ascending/descending) work correctly.
- Pagination controls (next/previous/page number) work correctly.

**AC-3 — Options section (flag enabled)**
- Enabling/disabling returns via the Symfony form saves correctly with a success flash message.
- Setting the validity period (number of days) saves correctly.
- Setting or clearing the return prefix saves correctly.

**AC-4 — Edit page (flag enabled)**
- Navigating from the listing to the edit page of a return works correctly (Symfony URL).
- Updating the return status via the Symfony form saves correctly with a success flash message.
- The returned products list is displayed correctly on the edit page.

**AC-6 — Feature flag promotion ⚠️**
- Once all scenarios pass with the feature flag enabled, the `merchandise_returns` feature flag is promoted from `experimental` to `stable` and `enabled` in the PrestaShop codebase (flag removed, Symfony controller becomes the only active route).

---

## Technical Notes

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Feature flag name | `merchandise_returns` |
| Migration PR | [#41527](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/41527) |
| Legacy controller | `AdminReturnController` |
| Legacy URL pattern | `/index.php?controller=AdminReturn` |
| Symfony controller | `MerchandiseReturnController` |
| Symfony URL pattern (listing) | `/index.php/sell/customer-service/merchandise-return/` |
| Symfony URL pattern (edit) | `/index.php/sell/customer-service/merchandise-return/{id}/edit` |
| BO menu path | `Customer Service > Merchandise Returns` |
| Spec reference (listing) | [Merchandise Returns listing spec](https://build.prestashop-project.org/prestashop-specs/1.7/back-office/customer-service/merchandise-returns/) |
| Spec reference (edit) | [Merchandise Returns edit spec](https://build.prestashop-project.org/prestashop-specs/1.7/back-office/customer-service/merchandise-returns/add-edit-merchandise-returns.html) |

**Run command:**
```bash
TEST_PATH="functional/BO/05_customerService/02_merchandiseReturns/*" \
URL_FO="<shop_url>" npm run test:specific
```

**Enable feature flag via CLI:**
```bash
php bin/console prestashop:feature-flag enable merchandise_returns
```

**Key implementation notes:**

- Use `beforeAll`/`afterAll` hooks to enable/disable the `merchandise_returns` feature flag cleanly, without affecting other test files in `05_customerService/` (customer service threads tests).
- The options section (enable/disable returns, validity period, prefix) is a **configuration form embedded at the bottom of the listing page** — not a separate page. Ensure the page object correctly handles scrolling to and interacting with this section on the Symfony page.
- To test the edit page (AC-4), a return request must exist. The test setup likely requires a prerequisite: returns must be enabled, and a completed order with a merchandise return request must be present. Verify the existing test's `beforeAll` setup and update it if the Symfony page changes the return request creation flow.
- The `06_merchandiseReturns.ts` file under `02_orders/01_orders/viewAndEditOrder/` is **out of scope** and must not be modified by this story.
- Review PR #41527 file changes for the exact Twig template selectors and Symfony route names before updating page objects.

---

## Definition of Done

- [ ] All test files under `05_customerService/02_merchandiseReturns/` pass with the `merchandise_returns` feature flag **enabled** (Symfony page)
- [ ] `02_orders/01_orders/viewAndEditOrder/06_merchandiseReturns.ts` is **unaffected**
- [ ] Tests run in the nightly CI pipeline on `develop`
- [ ] Feature flag `merchandise_returns` is promoted to **stable** and **enabled** and `AdminReturnController` is removed
- [ ] PR references the adapted test file(s) + the feature flag promotion commit

title: Replace window.prompt() with a modal when adding a page to Quick Access
issue_title: [Quick Access] Replace native prompt() dialog with a proper modal when adding a quick access link
issue_body:
**As** a back office user,  
**In order to** configure a quick access link properly when adding the current page,  
**I want** the native browser `prompt()` dialog to be replaced by a PrestaShop modal that lets me set the shortcut name **and** choose whether it opens in a new window.

---

## Context

### Current behaviour

When the user clicks **"Add current page to QuickAccess"** in the Quick Access dropdown, the BO triggers a native browser `window.prompt()` dialog:

```
Please name this shortcut: [________________]
```

This dialog:
- Is a **native browser UI element**, unstyled, inconsistent across browsers, and cannot be customised or translated contextually
- Offers **only a name input** — no way to set the "Open in new window" option at creation time
- Blocks the JavaScript thread in some contexts
- Cannot be tested reliably with Playwright (requires `page.on('dialog')` workarounds)

The relevant code is in:
```
admin-dev/themes/default/template/header.tpl
```
```javascript
var name = prompt('Please name this shortcut:', '{$quick_access_current_link_name.0|truncate:32}');
```

The Quick Access listing page (`Manage quick accesses`) already allows setting the "Open in new window" toggle when creating or editing a link. This option is **not exposed** at all in the dropdown "add" flow today, leading to a feature asymmetry.

### New behaviour

Clicking "Add current page to QuickAccess" opens a **PrestaShop modal** (using the existing `@PrestaShop/Admin/Components/Modal/` Twig component or the equivalent UIKit modal) containing:

- A **text input** pre-filled with the current page name (same default as the current `prompt()`)
- A **toggle switch** labelled "Open in new window" (defaulting to `off`)
- A **"Save"** button that submits the form via AJAX and closes the modal
- A **"Cancel"** button (or close icon) that dismisses the modal without action

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC-1 — Modal opens on click

- Clicking "Add current page to QuickAccess" in the Quick Access dropdown opens a PrestaShop modal.
- The native `window.prompt()` is no longer called anywhere in this flow.
- The modal is accessible (focus trap, `aria-modal`, `role="dialog"`, labelledby title).

### AC-2 — Name field

- The modal contains a text input labelled "Shortcut name" (or equivalent wording).
- The field is pre-filled with the current page name, truncated to 32 characters (same logic as the current `prompt()` default).
- The field is focused automatically when the modal opens.
- The field is required — the "Save" button is disabled (or inline validation is shown) when the field is empty.

### AC-3 — "Open in new window" toggle

- The modal contains a toggle switch labelled "Open in new window".
- The toggle defaults to **off**.
- When toggled on, the saved quick access link opens the page in a new browser tab (i.e., `new_window = 1` is sent to the AJAX endpoint).

### AC-4 — Save action

- Clicking "Save" submits the data via AJAX to the existing `AdminQuickAccesses` / Symfony `QuickAccessController` endpoint (same as the current flow, extended with the `new_window` parameter).
- On success:
  - The modal closes.
  - The dropdown list is refreshed to include the newly added link.
  - A success alert/flash is shown consistent with existing BO UX.
- On error:
  - The modal stays open.
  - An inline error message is shown.

### AC-5 — Cancel / close

- Clicking "Cancel" or the modal close icon dismisses the modal without creating a quick access link.
- The dropdown remains in its current state.
- Pressing `Escape` also dismisses the modal.

### AC-6 — Wording

The following wording keys are added to the `Admin.Navigation.Header` translation domain:

| Key | Default EN value |
|---|---|
| `Add to Quick Access` | `Add to Quick Access` (modal title) |
| `Shortcut name` | `Shortcut name` |
| `Open in new window` | `Open in new window` |
| `Save` | reuse existing key |
| `Cancel` | reuse existing key |

### AC-7 — No regression on existing quick access behaviour

- "Remove from Quick Access" still works as before (no modal, direct AJAX action).
- "Manage quick accesses" link still navigates to the listing page.
- Existing links in the dropdown still navigate correctly (incl. `new_window` behaviour).
- The `new_window` field in the Create/Edit form on the listing page is unaffected.

### AC-8 — AJAX endpoint compatibility

- The existing AJAX endpoint used by the "add" action (`action=GetUrl&method=add`) accepts the additional `new_window` parameter.
- If the Symfony-migrated controller (`QuickAccessController`, PR #41508) is in place, the endpoint on that side also handles the `new_window` parameter correctly.

---

## Technical Notes

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| File to modify (legacy header) | `admin-dev/themes/default/template/header.tpl` |
| Current mechanism | `window.prompt()` → AJAX to `AdminQuickAccesses?action=GetUrl&method=add` |
| Modal component | `@PrestaShop/Admin/Components/Modal/` or UIKit `ps-modal` |
| Toggle component | `SwitchType` Symfony form type / UIKit `ps-switch` |
| Translation domain | `Admin.Navigation.Header` |
| Related PR (listing page migration) | [#41508](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/41508) |

**Implementation notes:**

- The modal should be rendered server-side as a Twig include in `header.tpl` (or the equivalent Symfony Twig component for the migrated header), and shown/hidden via JavaScript — avoid generating the modal HTML dynamically in JS.
- The AJAX request to save the quick access link already exists. It only needs to be extended with the `new_window` parameter from the toggle value.
- If the Symfony Layout component for the header is already in use, implement the modal there rather than in the legacy `header.tpl`.
- The pre-filled name truncation (32 chars) is currently done in Smarty (`{$quick_access_current_link_name.0|truncate:32}`). Ensure the same truncation is applied in the Twig/JS equivalent.

---

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Native `window.prompt()` is removed from the "Add current page to QuickAccess" flow
- [ ] A PrestaShop modal opens with a name input (pre-filled, required) and an "Open in new window" toggle (default off)
- [ ] Save submits via AJAX with both `name` and `new_window` parameters, and the dropdown refreshes on success
- [ ] Cancel / Escape closes the modal without side effects
- [ ] Wording keys are added to `Admin.Navigation.Header` translation domain
- [ ] No regression on existing quick access dropdown behaviour (remove, navigate, manage)
- [ ] The modal is accessible (focus trap, ARIA attributes)
- [ ] A UI test covers the new modal flow (open, fill name, toggle new_window, save, verify link appears in dropdown)

issue_body: ## Context Part of the [Symfony migration project](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues/14770). The **"International > Taxes > Tax Rules"** section of the Back Office manages Tax Rules Groups and their associated per-country tax rules. It consists of two distinct pages: 1. **Tax Rules Groups — List page**: grid of all tax rules groups with enable/disable toggle and bulk actions. 2. **Tax Rules Group — Add / Edit page**: form to create or edit a group, plus an embedded sub-grid mapping countries to applicable tax rates. --- ## Pages & components in scope ### 1. Tax Rules Groups — List page **Legacy URL:** `?controller=AdminTaxRulesGroup` **Migrated URL:** `/index.php/improve/international/tax_rules_groups/` Contains: - A **grid listing** all tax rules groups, with columns: ID, Name, Enabled. - **Row actions:** Edit, Delete (with confirmation modal). - **Bulk actions:** Enable selection, Disable selection, Delete selection (with confirmation modal). ### 2. Tax Rules Group — Add / Edit page **Legacy URL:** `?controller=AdminTaxRulesGroup&addtax_rules_group` / `?controller=AdminTaxRulesGroup&id_tax_rules_group={id}&updatetax_rules_group` **Migrated URL:** `/index.php/improve/international/tax_rules_groups/new` / `/index.php/improve/international/tax_rules_groups/{id}/edit` Contains: - A **form** with Tax Rules Group name and enabled status. - An embedded **countries sub-grid** listing the tax rules applied per country (country, state/region, zip code, behaviour, tax, description). - **Row actions** on the sub-grid: Edit, Delete (with confirmation modal). --- ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Both pages are accessible via their Symfony URL and render correctly with the PrestaShop Twig layout (no legacy bridge / `@admin_legacy_cc`). - [ ] The Tax Rules Groups grid is fully functional: filtering, sorting, pagination, enable/disable toggle, bulk actions. - [ ] Delete actions (single row and bulk) on the list grid trigger a confirmation modal. - [ ] Delete actions (single row) on the countries sub-grid trigger a confirmation modal. - [ ] The Add / Edit form saves correctly (create and update). - [ ] The countries sub-grid in the Edit page is fully functional: add, edit, delete a country rule. - [ ] Commands and Queries are covered by Behat tests. --- ## Current migration status | Component | Status | Reference | |---|---|---| | Tax Rules Groups grid (list) | ✅ Merged | PR #15915 | | Bulk enable / disable status | ✅ Merged | PR #15915 | | Filters on the list | ✅ Merged | PR #15915, PR #28699 | | Delete confirmation modal — list (single row + bulk) | ✅ Merged | PR #28699 | | Add / Edit page (form + countries sub-grid) | ⚠️ Abandoned WIP | PR #15611 (closed) | | Delete confirmation modal — countries sub-grid | ⏳ Pending | Blocked on Add/Edit | | Behat tests | ⏳ Pending | — | --- ## Roadmap ### ✅ Completed - [x] Migrate the Tax Rules Groups listing, filters and bulk status actions → PR #15915 - [x] Add delete confirmation modal on list grid (single row and bulk delete) → PR #28699 ### ⚠️ Abandoned — needs to be picked up - [ ] Migrate the Add / Edit page (Tax Rules Group form + countries sub-grid) → A first implementation was started in PR #15611 (closed) by @RaimondasSapola. The Symfony routes are already defined: `/improve/international/tax_rules_groups/new` and `/improve/international/tax_rules_groups/{id}/edit`. The PR was closed without being merged due to lack of bandwidth. It can serve as a starting point for a new contribution. ### 🔧 Remaining (blocked on Add / Edit migration) - [ ] Add delete confirmation modal on the countries sub-grid (single row) - [ ] Remove legacy `AdminTaxRulesGroupController` and its legacy route alias - [ ] Cover Commands / Queries with Behat tests - [ ] Add controller survival test --- ## Check-List ### App layer #### Controller / routing - [x] All controller actions are migrated and protected with `@AdminSecurity` and `@DemoRestricted` annotations — **list page only** (PR #15915) - [ ] All controller actions are migrated and protected with `@AdminSecurity` and `@DemoRestricted` annotations — **Add/Edit page** (pending) - [x] All links targeting this page are updated using `_legacy_link` - [x] The new SF routes have `_legacy_link` and `_legacy_parameters` provided — **list page routes only** - [ ] The new SF routes have `_legacy_link` and `_legacy_parameters` provided — **Add/Edit page routes** (pending) - [x] Controller catches Domain Exceptions and translates them — list page - [ ] Controller catches Domain Exceptions and translates them — Add/Edit page - [ ] Add/Edit controller catches global Exception to handle `ModuleErrorException` #### Template - [x] Twig templates contain relevant blocks to allow partial extension by modules — list page (PR #15915) - [ ] Twig templates contain relevant blocks — Add/Edit page (pending) - [ ] Twig forms must have `form_rest()` and `form_errors()` (pending — Add/Edit) - [x] JS being used on the list page uses PageMap for selectors (PR #28699) - [ ] JS for the Add/Edit page uses PageMap for selectors (pending) - [x] `@PrestaShop` alias used instead of `PrestaShopBundle` — list page - title: Merchandise Returns : Cancel returns if the order return state is cancellable
issue_body:
> This issue has been migrated from the Forge. Read the [original ticket here](http://forge.prestashop.com/browse/BOOM-1069). - _**Reporter:**_ @vincentbz - _**Created at:**_ Mon, 18 Jul 2016 11:46:57 +0200

Hi,

As a customer, i've made an order that has been delivered.
I proceed to the product return, which is still "waiting for confirmation".

But in the order detail, the "product returned" is set to 1 when I ask to return, even if the return is rejected by the merchant.
If the merchant refuses it, it should be set to 0 again.
For the other statuses, the "returned" can stay to 1.

Thanks

--- #### Describe the bug As a customer, i've made an order that has been delivered. I proceed to the product return, which is still **waiting for confirmation**. In the other hand, the merchant refuses it. So the customer can see clearly that the return is denied and yet in the order details, the returned quantity is not updated. #### Expected behavior When the merchandise return is denied, the returned quantity must be set to 0 in the order details. #### Steps to Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Go to **BO** > **SELL** > **Customer Service** > **Merchandise Returns** 2. Enable returns 3. Go to **FO** > **Your account** > **Order history** page 4. Click on **Details** of an Order with status **Shipped** 5. Choose a product to return then click on **Request Return** button 6. Go to **BO** > **SELL** > **Customer Service** > **Merchandise Returns** 7. Change the return status to **Return denied** 8. Go to **FO** > **Your account** > **Merchandise Return** > check your return's status, it's denied 9. **Your account** > **Order history** > click on Details 10. See error, the quantity of returned product is still 1 (see screenshot below) **Screenshots** ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23308427/100858165-ed3a8300-348d-11eb-9777-66111e5ef8fe.png) #### Additional information * PrestaShop version: 1.7.6.9 & 1.7.7.0-rc.1 * PHP version: 7.2

Country Address format: replace legacy widget with Vue 3 visual builder
issue_body:
# Context As part of the legacy controller migration, the "Country" page migration must be completed. # Tests - The address format must contain at least the following values: phone_mobile, firstname, lastname, address1, city. - Any fields marked as mandatory for customer addresses (Customers > Addresses > Set required fields for this section) must be included in the address format # Claude design rework
We did a redesign of this component using Claude design, here is the result. **Collapse for more details** # GitHub issue summary — Country Address Format component ## What Replace the legacy "Address format" widget on the Country edit page with a modern Vue 3 visual builder, while keeping the same wire format and form name (drop-in BE compatibility). ## Why The current widget (a textarea + a row of "+ field" buttons split across 5 tabs + 4 reset buttons) is opaque: merchants don't see the result of their edits, can't reorder, and have no signal about which fields are required. Now that the rest of the Country form is migrated, this widget is the last thing standing in the way of the page. ## New UX (summary) - **Visual builder** with a left column of editable lines and a right-hand field picker. - **Live preview** below using a fixed sample customer (John DOE / 16 Main street / Paris). - **Drag and drop everywhere**: - Drag a field from the picker onto a line, between chips, or between lines. - Drag a chip from one line to another to move it. - Drag the left-hand grip of a line to reorder whole lines. - **Click `+`** on any picker pill to insert at the end of the last line (no DnD required). - **Required fields**: yellow warning banner with the missing-required tokens + an "Insert all missing →" shortcut. In the picker, required fields show a red asterisk (consistent with form labels). No hard-block on Save. - **Already-placed** fields are disabled in the picker (greyed out, ✓ instead of +). - **Search** sits above the picker tabs and searches across **all** objects at once. - **Visual / Raw** mode is rendered as nav-tabs above the editor — Raw mode is the current textarea for power users; the two sides stay in sync. - **Reset** is now a single dropdown (`Reset ▾`) replacing the 4 legacy buttons: *Default for this country / Last saved format / My current modified format / Clear*. ## Visual consistency The chip used to represent each token is the same component used by the **Combination Generator** (Catalog → Products) and the **input tags** field — same white pill, same `Key: value ×` format. All other UI (buttons, tabs, alerts, dropdown, toggles) reuses existing PrestaKit / legacy-theme components. **No new CSS for components that already exist.** ## BE contract The Symfony FormType renders a `
` with everything the JS needs (initial value, available fields per object, required fields list, default + last-registered formats, sample data, custom-address-fields URL, translations). A bootstrap function reads the data attributes and mounts the Vue app. The component owns a hidden `` so the form processor is unchanged. ## Out of scope / follow-ups - Hard-blocking Save on missing required fields (ask product). - Multi-record preview / preview record picker (could be a Phase 2). - Per-line "join with next line" affordance (explored, dropped — not worth the complexity).
# Validation plan — Country Address Format component
A short, UX-oriented checklist. Tick each box once you've tried it in the browser. **Collapse for more details** ## Visual builder — adding & removing fields - [ ] Click `+ firstname` in the picker → chip appears at the end of the last line - [ ] Drag a picker pill onto a chip → new chip is inserted at the drop point - [ ] Drag a picker pill into the empty gap between two lines → a new line is created at that index - [ ] Drag a picker pill onto an empty line → chip is appended to that line - [ ] Click a chip's `×` → only that chip is removed; line stays - [ ] Click a line's `×` (on hover) → whole line is removed - [ ] Try to add a field that's already placed → picker pill is disabled and shows `✓` instead of `+` ## Reordering - [ ] Drag a chip from one line to another → chip is moved (not duplicated); drop indicator visible - [ ] Drag a chip within the same line → chip reorders inside the line - [ ] Drag the left-hand line grip up or down → whole line is reordered; insertion indicator visible - [ ] Click `+ Add line` → an empty line is appended at the bottom ## Field picker - [ ] Search bar above the tabs filters across **all** objects at once (e.g. "post" finds `Address: postcode`) - [ ] While searching, tabs are visually de-emphasized - [ ] Clicking a tab while searching clears the search and focuses that tab - [ ] Tabs that contain a missing-required field show a red `*` after the label - [ ] Required fields show a red `*` next to the field name in the picker ## Required fields - [ ] When at least one required field is missing, the yellow warning banner shows on the left - [ ] The banner lists every missing field as a clickable chip; clicking one inserts that field - [ ] `Insert all missing →` adds all missing fields on a new line at the bottom - [ ] Once a required field is placed, the banner updates (or disappears if none left) - [ ] Saving works even when a required field is missing (no hard block) ## Visual ↔ Raw mode - [ ] `Visual editor` and `Raw template` are rendered as nav-tabs above the editor - [ ] Switching to Raw shows the current format as text - [ ] Editing the raw text and switching back updates the visual builder - [ ] Editing in Visual and switching to Raw shows the same value ## Reset dropdown - [ ] `Reset ▾` opens a dropdown with 4 entries - [ ] **Default for this country** restores the PrestaShop built-in default - [ ] **Last saved format** restores what's currently in the database - [ ] **My current modified format** restores the local in-progress draft - [ ] **Clear format** empties all lines (with a small inline confirmation) ## Live preview - [ ] The preview renders below (or beside) the editor with the fixed sample customer - [ ] Each line of the preview reflects the current format - [ ] Empty lines (all tokens empty for the sample) are skipped - [ ] Editing a line updates the preview immediately ## Visual consistency with the rest of the BO - [ ] Chips look identical to the ones used in the **Combination Generator** modal and the **input-tags** field (white pill, `Key: value ×`, same border/shadow) - [ ] Buttons, dropdowns, tabs, alert/banner, search input, and toggles are reused from the existing design system — nothing custom-styled - [ ] Icons come from Material Symbols Outlined as elsewhere in the BO ## Keyboard & accessibility - [ ] Tab order is logical: mode tabs → banner → lines → Add line → search → picker tabs → pills → Reset - [ ] Focus rings are visible on every focusable element - [ ] On a focused line grip, ↑ / ↓ moves the line up/down - [ ] On a focused chip, Alt+←/→ reorders within the line; Alt+↑/↓ moves between lines - [ ] On a focused picker pill, Enter inserts the field - [ ] Required-field asterisks are read out as "required" by screen readers - [ ] Long translations (DE/FR) and long custom-field names wrap predictably without breaking layout
